text: Most important: this consult is mostly a procedure walkthrough (assessment, bougie technique, confirmation, failed-airway pathway, cricothyrotomy), not a memorised resuscitation sequence. The strip is the best faithful 7-tile reduction, but the bougie and cricothyrotomy tiles are step lists, not single actions. The cricothyrotomy tile holds steps 2 to 9 of the consult's 10 steps (eight-line cap), so it omits step 1 (stabilize larynx) and step 10 (confirm with waveform capnography). A physician should decide whether this consult belongs on a RAPID strip at all.

Time-critical content NOT on the strip: video laryngoscopy for all intubations and bougie-first for predicted difficult airways (critical actions on dab-start; only the kit and assessment lines are quoted); RSI drugs and doses (all of dab-standard-rsi and dab-bougie-rsi; drugs are left off, not drafted); the option to consider awake intubation in extreme-risk patients; Cormack-Lehane grade and when the bougie is indicated; adjuncts (jaw thrust, ELM, BURP) and common errors; the green-zone rescue (supraglottic airway, call for help, do not make repeated blind attempts); SGA bridge; cricothyroid membrane landmarks and laryngeal handshake; ETCO2 check after cric; post-intubation and post-cric care. Critical actions left off or only partly shown: 'Feel for tracheal clicks' (the consult itself calls clicks unreliable, so that line is quoted with its caution); 'Hold bougie in place while loading ETT over it' (the consult's technique node has no such line; not on the strip); 'Use video laryngoscopy for all intubations' and 'Use bougie-first technique' (dab-start lines not quoted). Tile order follows the consult's flow for a failed attempt (kit, LEMON, bougie, attempt limit, capnography, failed airway, cric), not the critical-actions list order; in the consult, capnography is reached directly after a successful tube pass, so the physician should check whether capnography should sit before the attempt-limit tile (the checker raises order flags on both). Reviewer additions: the bougie tile (eight-line cap) leaves off step 5 'Remove bougie once ETT at appropriate depth', step 1 'Laryngoscopy', the 90-degree ETT rotation when it catches on arytenoids, and the adjunct maneuvers. The failed-airway tile shows the Green Zone line (adequate oxygenation by ANY lifeline: time to think, plan, call for help) beside the CICO line, but the green-zone rescue itself (supraglottic airway, do NOT make repeated blind intubation attempts, call anesthesiology/ENT) is not on the strip, so declaring failed airway on this strip does not by itself mean cut.

The critical action 'Call for help early if failed attempt - do not exceed 3 attempts' says to call for help, but the attempt-count node does not say so; it only limits attempts and lists what to change between them. 'Call for help early' appears in the consult only under awake intubation and green-zone rescue. Nothing was added.

The consult's critical action says 'Hold bougie in place while loading ETT over it', but no line of the technique node says this. The step 'Slide pre-lubricated ETT over bougie' is quoted instead. Also: the technique warns tracheal clicks are unreliable, and the 'Do NOT preload' warning sits on the equipment node, not the technique node.

The cricothyrotomy tile jumps to dab-cric-go but quotes only the technique node, because the eight-line cap forced a choice between the announcement and the steps. The 'cannot oxygenate' trigger is quoted on the failed-airway tile instead. No drugs are on this strip, so no drug-store comparison applies.

The bougie tile's condition 'Predicted difficult airway' is the consult's bougie-first trigger, but the consult also calls for the bougie when the laryngoscopic view is poor (CL IIb-IV, dab-rsi-complete), which is not on the strip. Physician to confirm the condition wording is acceptable.
